title: How Does Soap Kill Germs?
short_title: Why Soap Destroys Germs (And Why 20 Seconds Matters)
description: Soap does not just wash germs off, it can rip many of them apart. Here is the simple science of soap molecules, and why washing for 20 seconds works.
comment: How long do you really wash your hands? Be honest! 😄

scenes.text: Why can plain soap destroy germs, and why do doctors say to wash for twenty seconds?
Many germs, like flu viruses, wear a greasy outer coat. That coat holds them together.
A soap molecule has two ends. One end loves water. The other end loves grease.
The greasy tails stab into the germ's coat and pull it apart, like pulling threads out of a sweater.
Soap also grabs germs and dirt on your skin, and water washes them all away. Scrubbing gives the soap time to work. That is why twenty seconds.
So for everyday washing, plain soap and water work great.
